blocks.orig: Chumbe Island Coral Park is an award-winning private nature reserve. It is located only a few kilometers off the southwest coast of Zanzibar, near Stone Town. The reserve includes a fully protected coral reef sanctuary and a forest reserve. It harbors rare wildlife, a visitor and education center, a small eco-lodge, nature walks and historical monuments. All buildings and operations are based on eco-technology aiming at zero impact on the environment.
blocks.html: Chumbe Island Coral Park is a privately run nature reserve that has collected several awards. It sits a few kilometres off Zanzibar's southwest coast, not far from Stone Town. Within the park lie a fully protected coral reef sanctuary and a forest reserve sheltering rare species, plus a visitor and education centre, a small eco-lodge, nature trails and historical monuments. Every building and daily operation relies on eco-technology designed to leave no footprint on its surroundings.

blocks.orig: Accommodation on Chumbe Island is – in many aspects – something really special. Because there is only one lodge on the island with just 7 bungalows, it feels quite spacious – even when the place is at its maximum capacity. The design of these 7 bungalows is so brilliant that they provide both privacy and a sense of freedom of living in the open. All bungalows overlook the sea and it takes just 30 seconds to stroll from your bungalow hammock to the warm tropical ocean lapping at your feet. Even dining on the island is with great consideration for the natural marine ecology. Not only will you get delicious African, Zanzibarian, Arabic and Indian dishes – they also have a seafood purchasing policy that ensures sustainable seafood harvesting. Chumbe Island is the place where luxury meets sustainability!
blocks.html: Staying on Chumbe Island is, in many ways, a genuinely unusual experience. The island has a single lodge with only 7 bungalows, so it never feels crowded – not even when every bungalow is occupied. The 7 bungalows are so cleverly designed that you get privacy as well as the feeling of living out in the open. Each one looks out over the sea, and the walk from the hammock at your bungalow to the warm tropical water takes no more than 30 seconds. Even the meals are prepared with the marine environment firmly in mind. You will enjoy delicious African, Zanzibari, Arabic and Indian dishes, while a seafood purchasing policy guarantees that everything is harvested sustainably. On Chumbe Island, luxury and sustainability go hand in hand!

blocks.orig: The island’s guest lodges are constructed in an eco-friendly way. It’s what Robinson Crusoe could only have dreamt about! These designs have near to zero impact on the environment of Chumbe Island. The technology includes rainwater catchment, photovoltaic energy, solar water heating, composting toilets and vegetative grey-water filtration. During your stay, you can be sure that you are keeping the island pristine.
blocks.html: The lodges where guests sleep were built with the environment in mind. Robinson Crusoe could only have dreamt of a place like this! Thanks to their design, they leave hardly any trace on Chumbe Island. Rainwater is collected, electricity comes from photovoltaic panels, water is heated by the sun, the toilets are composting ones and grey water is cleaned by plants. So throughout your visit you can be confident that the island remains untouched.

blocks.orig: Please note that Chumbe Island is closed every year between April 1st and June 3rd.
blocks.html: Bear in mind that Chumbe Island closes each year from April 1st until June 3rd.

blocks.orig: In order to reach Chumbe Island, you have to take a boat from Stone Town in Zanzibar.
blocks.html: Getting to Chumbe Island means taking a boat that departs from Stone Town on Zanzibar.
